title: Text helpers
description:
Write four string functions:

```javascript
function capitalize(text) { }       // "the lord of the RINGS" -> "The lord of the rings": first character upper case, the rest lower case
function truncate(text, max) { }    // at most max characters; if cut, the last character is "…"
function countChars(text) { }       // the number of characters, counting an emoji as one
function receiptLine(item, price) { }   // item padded to 12 characters, price with 2 decimals right-aligned in 8
```

`truncate("Hello, world", 6)` is `"Hello…"`; text that fits is returned unchanged. `receiptLine("tea", 2.5)` is `"tea             2.50"`.
hints: `text.slice(0, 1)` is the first character (or `""` for empty text, where `text[0]` would be `undefined`), and `text.slice(1)` is the rest.

`truncate` must choose between two results. The conditional operator does that in one expression: `condition ? whenTrue : whenFalse`, for example `text.length <= max ? text : ...` (lesson 1.05 covers it with `if`).
`[...text]` splits a string into characters properly, keeping an emoji's two halves together.
`padEnd(12)` adds spaces on the right up to 12 characters (and does nothing if the text is longer); `toFixed(2)` gives two decimals as a string.
